topic: retrieval-augmented generation: evaluation, robustness, citation grounding, context efficiency
topic_note: Chosen 2026-09-17, replacing six 2020-2026 lithium-ion cathode papers inherited from the demo corpus that was removed with the `global` tenant. Those were off-topic for an AI-engineering portfolio and parsed badly -- subscripted chemical formulas did not survive Docling, so a whole class of question was unanswerable for reasons that had nothing to do with retrieval.
seed_tenant_id_note: Pinned, not minted. `upload_doc_id` salts the content digest with the tenant id, so every doc_id -- and therefore every chunk_id -- in `chunk_manifest.json` and `qa_dataset.jsonl` is a function of this value. A freshly minted tenant would rebuild the same corpus under different chunk ids and silently invalidate every golden reference.
